approval_note: The committee cannot approve. PASS means no auditor found anything to veto on its own axis with the evidence it was given. Reading that as approval is a caller's policy -- pre-registration.md 6a -- and its error rate is unmeasured.

auditors.confidence_note: The strategy only reads prior-session state (self._prior_atrs) and accumulates current-session state from ctx.closed bars, with the decision executed after ctx.actionable; I could not verify harness semantics for ctx.bars[self.interval] (whether it is the just-closed bar or the forming bar) but the code pattern and the docstring's 'entry on the bar close' suggest closed-bar semantics and nothing in the code reaches for future data, the scorer, the dataset, or the split.

The gate rejected (p=1.0, observed best 0.012 far below the null-max 5% quantile 0.46) and every view is coherent with that: 0 uncorrected/BH/Holm discoveries, negative deflation margin, p nowhere near the resolution floor, and the winner's Sortino rests on 196 downside sessions out of 384 and 4528 trades, so no degenerate denominator or session concentration is in play; what I cannot see is the prior-campaign look count, the per-session return series behind the concentration check, and any out-of-sample evidence (validation was not run), none of which matters for a result that claims nothing.

reasons: Costs decide the outcome: commission paid is 913.1 points against gross P&L of 1187.75 points — 77% of gross is consumed by commission alone. Net P&L of 274.65 points is entirely a residue of cost assumptions.

Per-trade gross edge is 0.262 points (1187.75 / 4528) while commission per round trip is 0.202 points. That leaves 0.06 points of gross edge per trade above commission — well inside any plausible spread. fill_model_spread is null, so no explicit spread was applied; NQ's minimum tick is 0.25 points (~$5), and any realistic round-trip spread of ~0.25 points on top of commission (total cost ~0.45 points) flips the strategy negative in real terms. Reported positive net P&L is an artifact of zero-spread fills.

Reported avg_holding_period_ns ≈ 834 seconds ≈ 13.9 minutes exceeds the strategy's own stated 10-minute deadline (hold_minutes=10, deadline enforced via ctx.close()). Either the deadline is not being enforced as stated or the reported holding period is measured differently from the rule the docstring claims to implement; either way the economics of a 'short-horizon fade' are not the economics the code is actually running.
auditors.confidence_note: No per-session P&L distribution, no per-month/hour breakdown, and no evidence about how much of the 274.65-point net survives a realistic spread model were provided; concentration risk flagged in the pre-registration could not be checked.

reasons: Time concentration: 2024-11 (+876.55) and 2025-01 (+846.10) alone produce +1722.65 against a total of roughly +275; removing those two of fifteen months flips the total to approximately -1248. The result is the sample's two best months, not the sample.

Session-level concentration: profit_concentration_top5pct = 5.83, i.e. the best ~19 of 384 sessions contribute 583% of net profit — meaning the remaining ~365 sessions lose about 4.8x the total profit. Remove those sessions and the campaign is a substantial loser. best_session_share of 5.5% is fine, but the top-5% figure is not.

Hour-of-day concentration: hours 15 (+938) and 16 (+610) UTC alone account for +1548 against +275 net (≈563% of total); excluding those two of 24 hours the total goes to approximately -1273. No structural reason is offered for why US-cash-session hours should persistently hold the entire edge.

Weekday concentration: Thursday alone contributes +1082.6 against +275 net (≈394% of total), while Monday (-707) and Friday (-1011) are both deeply negative. Excluding Thursday flips the campaign sign.

Loss-rate structure: downside_sessions = 196 out of sessions_with_exposure = 253, i.e. roughly 77% of sessions lose money while a small tail of big winners pays for everything. Combined with the concentration figures above, the reported net is produced by a handful of outlier sessions rather than a broad, repeatable edge.
auditors.confidence_note: Per-trade and per-session distributions (return histograms, holding-period and instrument breakdowns, filter/config attribution) were not provided, so I cannot tell which specific rules or symbols drive the concentrated tail — but the month/hour/weekday and top-5% concentration alone are sufficient to call the result narrow.
